independent.summary: The sweep is now async and holds a stale `client` reference across the `await client.sessionAlive(...)`; if `closeStreamsForSession`/`closeStreamsForUser` (logout or account deletion) ends that same connection during the in-flight store read, the sweep then writes a keep-alive ping to an already-`end()`ed response. Write-after-end is reported asynchronously (an `error` emitted on the ServerResponse), so the surrounding synchronous `try/catch` does not cover it and nothing listens for it. Re-checking `clients.has(clientId)` after the await would close the window; the pre-change sweep was fully synchronous and could not interleave.

The refusal frame uses the SSE event name `error`, which browsers dispatch on the EventSource as an event of type "error" — i.e. straight into `es.onerror`. The client this repo ships (`client/src/composables/useEvents.js`) never reads `e.data` in `onerror`; it closes and reconnects after 3s, so an over-cap tab loops `GET /events` every 3 seconds indefinitely and the refusal reason is indistinguishable from "the wifi dropped" — exactly the outcome the 200+frame choice is documented as avoiding (docs/api.md, Decision Log). Reconnect/backoff is out of scope for the item, but a distinct event name (e.g. `stream:error`) would at least make the reason readable.

grades.reason: `sessionAlive` is not a local symbol — the route passes `req.app.locals.sessionAlive`, which `createApp` defines at server/src/app.js:93, and `addClient`/`streamErrorFrame` are imported at line 4.
`openStream` records `status: res.statusCode`, and every caller asserts it: `openReadyStream` does `assert.equal(stream.status, 200)` and the refusal test asserts 200 plus the exact error frame.
`removeClient` deletes the entry from the `clients` Map synchronously, and `openFor` recounts on every `addClient`, so the slot is free immediately — no sweep is involved in that path.

triageGrades.reason: The change edits `POST /auth/logout` and `DELETE /auth/account`, and adds post-connect session re-validation built from the session store in app.js.
No credential handling is added; the new env vars are a numeric cap and a log level, and BEARER_TOKEN is only referenced in comments/bucket keying.
Nothing touches billing, usage metering or cost paths.
The change deletes/overwrites no data — it closes sockets and adds logging to the existing deletion route — and the cited evidence (broadcaster.js:20) is a doc comment about the clients map.
No outbound third-party calls; the only new dependency is the already-configured session store lookup.
No version, build, CI or deploy-pipeline change; the two new env vars are optional with in-code defaults.

summary: All three local findings are false positives — two misread the code (an injected `app.locals` lookup and tests that do assert status) and one invents a sweep dependency that does not exist — while the triage was right except for calling the change destructive.
